raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies removable partitions already assembled and offers an opportunity to check the ordered contents before dispatch. Its strongest support is repeated three-compartment completion in seven to nine minutes, seven of ten customers succeeding unaided, and no recorded damage claims. Nevertheless, the combined median is 11 minutes, and five missing/incorrect-part reports indicate a completeness concern without establishing its frequency independently. Mixed batches contain every very slow order, but layout complexity could confound that association. A concrete limit on a width-only insertion explanation is D2-O5: widths overlap between first-attempt and retry parts. Neither this overlap nor the absence of damage claims proves the present geometry optimal. The stipulated evidence does not establish pilot success.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a reusable, order-specific staging template with partition counts and exterior-color confirmation could reduce selection and checking overhead while retaining full assembly.
openings.delta: Add a visible completeness check before insertion to the shared-bin workflow; preserve every accepted layout and color.
openings.prediction: Against matched layouts, total labor including staging falls mainly in selection/checking, with fewer content discrepancies; insertion time changes little.
openings.probe: Alternate current and staged work on spare-board samples, balancing worker and layout. Time every phase, count all preparation labor, and independently compare packed contents with slips. Cost the reusable template and reserve trial time before changing accepted-order production.
assumptions: The template fits the single bench.
Initial expense stays within 500 and recurring material increment within 0.40.
Trial and rollout preserve the delivery date; unchanged geometry and removable joints preserve capacity and footprint.

openings.claim: Do insertion retries follow a particular part, slot, or insertion orientation?
openings.delta: Distinguish local mating or handling effects from partition width alone before changing cutting templates.
openings.prediction: Part-linked failures persist across compatible slots; slot-linked failures transfer across parts; orientation-linked failures change with orientation.
openings.probe: Use spare samples to cross-test compatible parts and slots in permissible orientations, counterbalancing trial order and worker. Record first-attempt success and visible wear; keep accepted-order parts untouched.
assumptions: Compatible pairings exist without changing the ordered arrangement.
Practice and wear may confound repeated trials.
A bounded sample test fits available working time.

raw.assessment: Model payment against the fixed 60-order cohort and all three success thresholds, retaining rearrangeability. Every accepted layout and color counts. Observations establish no causal mechanism; both alternatives remain hypotheses.

openings.claim: Paid for customers achieving their ordered arrangement, the provider might supply counted, unassembled order kits with order-specific placement diagrams replacing the generic diagram.
openings.delta: Remove workshop insertion while retaining selected components, footprint, capacity and reversible connections. Outcome payment makes instruction quality economically relevant.
openings.prediction: Workshop time could fall while customer success worsens if insertion effort or short-partition ambiguity dominates. Gaming could shift labor to customers, coach participants or exclude nonrespondents.
openings.probe: Compare five sample kits and five assembled samples using ten participants, balancing layouts. Independently check contents and observe unaided arrangement within the same ten-minute window; record workshop stages and customer time separately. This screens feasibility, not pilot success.
assumptions: The sales promise permits unassembled delivery.
Retain accepted colors, counts and date; reject implementation exceeding 500 initial or 0.40 recurring cost.

openings.claim: Paid for complete delivery across the fixed cohort, the provider might stage order-specific component sets and assemble consecutive same-layout orders using reusable bench trays.
openings.delta: Retain assembled delivery; change selection and sequencing. Payment requires each packed set to match its original order, including rare colors and complex layouts.
openings.prediction: If switching contributes to delays, selection and insertion times should improve without more packing mismatches. Gaming could postpone six-compartment orders or omit staging labor from timing.
openings.probe: Use the remaining five samples for matched mixed-sequence and grouped-sequence dry runs, counterbalancing worker order. Include staging, checking and packing in elapsed and worker-minute totals; independently audit layout and color. Track the entire cohort's completion schedule.
assumptions: Trays fit the single bench and 500 initial budget, with recurring additions at most 0.40 per order.
Grouping permits every accepted order to meet the fixed date.
Unchanged product dimensions, capacity and connections preserve rearrangeability.
Customer placement ambiguity may persist; faster production alone cannot establish success.

openings.claim: Order staging may reduce selection/checking overhead.
openings.probe: Alternate matched staged/current samples; balance worker/layout; time all phases/preparation; audit contents/color.

openings.claim: Retries may follow part, slot or orientation.
openings.probe: Counterbalance worker/order across pairings/orientations; record first-attempt success/wear.

openings.claim: Outcome payment may favor counted unassembled kits and ordered-layout diagrams.
openings.discriminator: Workshop savings versus customer insertion burden.
openings.probe: Ten participants: five kits/five assembled; balance layouts, audit contents; observe unaided arrangement within ten minutes; separate workshop/customer times.
openings.uncertainty: Short-partition ambiguity; coaching/nonrespondent exclusions distort results.

openings.claim: Complete-cohort payment may favor staging trays and same-layout sequencing.
openings.discriminator: Less switching improves selection/insertion without mismatches.
openings.probe: Remaining five samples: matched mixed/grouped runs, counterbalanced workers; count staging/checking/packing in elapsed time/worker-minutes; audit layout/color/cohort schedule.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity confounding; deferred complex orders/omitted labor; placement ambiguity persists.

post_distill.decision: Screen within 15 samples/available time. Require 30x20 cm footprint, same assortment, removable partitions, accepted counts/colors/date; initial <=500, recurring increment <=0.40. All 60 orders count: >=98% complete, median workshop <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided arrangement. Synthetic observations and small screens establish no pilot success.
